---
title: "summarise() reuses the columns it has just created"
ref: TDY-08
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'summarise(df, x = mean(x), s = sd(x))$s'
reponse: 'NA'
attendu: "the mean and the standard deviation of x"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2026)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

measures <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3, 10))
summarise(measures, x = mean(x), s = sd(x))
```
:::

## Why

`summarise()` and `mutate()` evaluate their expressions in order, and each new column is visible to the following ones. Here, `x` is first replaced by its mean, a single value. `sd()` is then computed on that single value, and the standard deviation of a single value is `NA`.

This is by design, and often handy. The trap appears when you reuse the name of an existing column.

## The remedy

Give the result a new name, or compute the standard deviation first.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

summarise(measures, mean = mean(x), s = sd(x))
```
:::
